status_summary: Executive Order 14181 (signed 2025-01-24, published 2025-01-31) directs Reclamation to deliver more Central Valley Project water, including by increasing storage and conveyance, and to identify California water-supply and storage projects. On 2026-01-23 Interior approved the record of decision for the 1.5 million acre-foot Sites Reservoir, with Reclamation funding up to 25 percent of cost, and reported that operational changes under the order delivered more than 200,000 additional acre-feet of water to the Central Valley Project within a year, partly attributed to favorable hydrology. Reclamation also signed a Record of Decision on 2025-12-04 for an updated long-term operation plan for the Central Valley Project, which it describes as responding to the order and as allowing 130 to 180 thousand acre-feet more in annual project deliveries depending on hydrology, and its 2026-03-24 and 2026-05-19 releases raised 2026 allocations while crediting operational improvements supported by the order. These are operational steps for California; the release of 2025-12-04 describes no change to reservoir storage. The order does not mention the 2018 western water memorandum, and no action on water control manuals, working-group consolidation, forecast-informed operations or WIFIA was found, so the match is partial and limited to California.

title: Expand western water storage and modernize reservoir operations at Reclamation
uncertainties: The 2018 memorandum is not in the order text, and a news search found no reinstatement. The Federal Register page for the order lists two later executive orders of 2026-01-23 (EO 14377 and EO 14378) as related notes; their content was not read, and one search did not identify them. The release attributes part of the added water to favorable hydrology rather than to the order alone. Reclamation's forecast-informed operations work was not found beyond a state council letter that was not relied on. Whether storage projects outside California advanced was not searched in detail. The three Reclamation releases were read on usbr.gov (2025-12-04, 2026-03-24 and 2026-05-19); the long-term operation plan Record of Decision itself and the Action 5 terms were not opened, and the share of 2026 allocation increases due to operations rather than hydrology is not stated in the releases. A search for Sites Reservoir developments after 2026-01-23 and for water control manual or forecast-informed operations actions under the order found nothing further from a federal source. The 2026-05-19 release cites improved storage, spring runoff and coordinated reservoir management alongside the order, so the allocation increases are not attributed to the order alone.
